name: Blackbar
one_liner: A browser-resident redaction engine: a fine-tuned PII/PHI span-tagger runs locally on WebGPU, finds every FRCP 5.2 / HIPAA identifier across a 200-page scanned or native PDF, burns true redactions, then re-reads its own output file to prove nothing survived — and the document never leaves the machine.
product_form: Standalone web app (browser-resident, local inference; no upload endpoint for document bytes exists). UX: drag a PDF onto the page and watch the local model tag spans and paint candidate boxes over the rendered pages, each with a category and confidence chip; review in one pass, hit Export, and the app rebuilds the PDF with the underlying glyphs deleted (rasterize fallback), then runs a verification pass that re-extracts text from the file it just made and re-runs detection, refusing to hand over the file if any identifier survived.
ai_core: A specialized fine-tuned model, not a frontier API call — mandatory, because the defining constraint is that bytes cannot leave the device. Two stages, both local ONNX via transformers.js (WebGPU support confirmed at https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers.js/en/index, fetched 2026-08-20): (1) page render plus OCR for scanned pages, producing character-level text with bounding boxes; (2) the product proper — a compact encoder token-classifier (base: a ~150-400M-parameter encoder of the ModernBERT-base / DeBERTa-v3-small class, exported to ONNX at q4/q8 per that page's documented dtype options) LoRA-fine-tuned to tag spans by identifier class (SSN/TIN, DOB, minor's name, financial-account number, MRN, address, phone, email, plate, device ID), unioned with deterministic high-precision recognizers (SSN area/group validity, Luhn for card numbers, ABA routing checksum) so the model only has to catch what regex structurally cannot: names of minors, addresses in OCR-mangled text, account numbers written in prose. DATASET, assembled autonomously: (a) public-domain document text at scale from CourtListener bulk data — courts, dockets, opinion clusters, full opinion text, CSV on S3, 'free of known copyright restrictions', Public Domain Mark, regenerated quarterly on the last day of March/June/September/December (https://wiki.free.law/c/courtlistener/help/api/bulk-data/bulk-legal-data, fetched 2026-08-20); (b) a generator that injects synthetic identifiers (Faker plus format-valid SSNs, routing numbers, MRNs) into that text at KNOWN character spans, typesets it into realistic filing and medical-form layouts, renders to PDF, then rasterizes with scan degradation (skew, JPEG noise, speckle, 200dpi fax) and re-OCRs — so every training page carries a perfect label at both character AND pixel level, at zero acquisition cost and unlimited volume. Labels are never hand-made and never bought; they are a by-product of generation. Target: 2-5M labeled pages across ~40 layout families, regenerable from scratch on every corpus refresh.
why_now: Two capabilities, both post-2023. (1) In-browser GPU inference became real: WebGPU now sits at 85.56% global support (83.99% + 1.57%), Chrome 113+, Edge 113+, iOS Safari 26.0+ full, Safari desktop 26.0+ partial — https://caniuse.com/webgpu, fetched 2026-08-20 — and transformers.js runs ONNX models on device:'webgpu' with q4/q8 quantization for token classification, NER and document-image-to-text (https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers.js/en/index, fetched 2026-08-20). Before this, private client-side redaction meant a desktop install, which is exactly why every incumbent below is a server. (2) Fine-tuning a specialized tagger became a rounding error: Together AI charges $0.48 per 1M training tokens for LoRA SFT up to 16B with a $4.00 job minimum (https://www.together.ai/pricing, fetched 2026-08-20). A capability that in 2022 was a regex-plus-CRF library with poor recall on OCR-noisy scans is now a 150MB file that runs in a tab.
buyer: Solo and small-firm US litigators — every exhibit filed in federal court must comply with FRCP 5.2(a): only the last four digits of an SSN/TIN, the year of birth only, a minor's initials only, and the last four digits of a financial-account number (https://www.law.cornell.edu/rules/frcp/rule_5.2, fetched 2026-08-20; rule adopted 2007-04-30, effective 2007-12-01). Adjacent: solo behavioral-health and allied-health practices handling records requests, small-district FOIA and public-records clerks, SMB HR. Self-serve reachable by card-swipe web app with no install and no IT review — and critically no vendor security questionnaire, because there is no vendor to review when nothing is transmitted. HONEST GAP: I could not fetch a population count for US solo practitioners today (this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted at 200/200), so the NUMBER of buyers is NOT sourced and must be verified before this idea advances. What IS sourced is that money already moves at four distinct price points — see market_evidence.
market_evidence: Redaction is a paid category today, priced from consumer to government, all fetched 2026-08-20: (a) Redactable sells AI-powered redaction at $19/mo for 15 documents and $99/mo for 150 documents — roughly $0.66-$1.27 per document — with OCR for scanned files and redaction certificates (https://www.redactable.com/pricing); (b) CaseGuard sells Doc Suite at $279/user/month, Media Suite $299, Ultimate $379, billed annually per seat (https://caseguard.com/pricing/); (c) Adobe bundles manual redaction into Acrobat Pro for teams at $23.99/month, $287.88/year (https://www.adobe.com/acrobat/pricing/business.html); (d) iLovePDF ships a manual Redact PDF tool inside a $5/mo annual ($9/mo monthly) Premium plan (https://www.ilovepdf.com/pricing). A market where the same verb sells at $5 and at $379 per seat per month has an unserved middle — and the fact that Redactable meters documents at all is direct evidence that per-document cloud inference cost is the binding constraint on their packaging, which is precisely the constraint local inference removes.
incumbents: Five closest, each with pricing fetched 2026-08-20, each leaving the same gap. (1) Redactable — $19/mo/15 docs, $99/mo/150 docs, Enterprise custom; 'AI Powered Redaction', OCR, audit logs and certificates; explicitly cloud, documents processed through their servers rather than locally (https://www.redactable.com/pricing). Gap: upload required, volume metered. (2) CaseGuard — $279-$379/user/month, unlimited document and image redaction with AI batch processing; the pricing page references 'cloud-based AI hours' and reserves offline mode for Enterprise only (https://caseguard.com/pricing/). Gap: government/enterprise price point, per-seat, local processing paywalled. (3) Adobe Acrobat Pro for teams — $23.99/mo, redaction to permanently remove sensitive visible information (https://www.adobe.com/acrobat/pricing/business.html). Gap: manual mark-and-apply; the human still has to FIND every SSN across 200 pages, which is the actual labour. (4) iLovePDF — Premium $5/mo annual or $9/mo monthly; Redact PDF is manual, one document per task, processed on their servers across 7-11 regions (https://www.ilovepdf.com/pricing). Gap: manual, one-at-a-time, server-side. (5) Microsoft Presidio — MIT licence, 10.6k GitHub stars, includes a module for redacting PII text in images and DICOM (https://github.com/microsoft/presidio). Gap: a Python/PySpark developer library deployed via Docker to Kubernetes with regex+spaCy recognizers and no browser path; a solo attorney cannot use it, and its recall on OCR-noisy scanned filings is exactly what a fine-tune improves. Chrome Web Store install counts are not applicable — this ships as a web app, not an extension, deliberately (see risks/AP6).
moat: Three layers, none of them a prompt. (1) The assembled corpus and its generator: millions of pages of public-domain legal and administrative text (CourtListener bulk, quarterly-refreshed, Public Domain Mark) with format-valid synthetic identifiers injected at known character AND pixel spans, then typeset, rendered, degraded and re-OCR'd — a labelled distribution of PII as it appears AFTER bad OCR, which is where regex and generalists fail and which cannot be scraped because it does not exist in the wild with labels. (2) The eval harness, which is the certifiable asset: per-identifier-class recall at fixed precision on held-out layout families, with a published floor per class (SSN and account-number recall reported to three decimals; minor-name recall reported separately because it is the hard class), regenerated automatically on each corpus refresh. This is the AP1 answer in its strongest form — nobody can certify Claude or Gemini on this task for this buyer, because certifying it requires running the buyer's privileged documents through it, which is the exact thing they are paying not to do. (3) The output-verification pass — the product re-reads the file it produced and re-runs detection against it — which converts the eval from a marketing number into a per-document guarantee and is the mechanism behind A3. Why the fine-tune beats a frontier generalist: not on raw language ability, but on (i) admissibility, it runs where the document already is; (ii) character-level span plus bbox output over 200 pages in one pass rather than prose; (iii) measured recall on OCR-degraded identifiers; (iv) $0 per document, which is what lets the plan say 'unlimited' where Redactable must say '15'.
inference_economics: AP4, and it is the wedge. Marginal inference cost per document: $0.00 — a ~150-400M-parameter encoder exported to ONNX at q4 is a ~150-200MB one-time browser download, cached thereafter, executed on the viewer's own GPU (dtype options q4/q8/fp16/fp32 documented at https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers.js/en/index, fetched 2026-08-20; WebGPU reach 85.56% per https://caniuse.com/webgpu, fetched 2026-08-20; a WASM q8 fallback covers Firefox, where WebGPU is still disabled by default). Training cost is trivial and repeatable: Together AI LoRA SFT is $0.48 per 1M tokens up to 16B, $1.20 for full fine-tune, with a $4.00 job minimum (https://www.together.ai/pricing, fetched 2026-08-20) — a 50M-token tagger tune is roughly $24, so twenty full retraining iterations across the entire roadmap cost under $500. Contrast the cloud path: a frontier VLM pass over a 200-page scanned deposition costs dollars per document, which is visibly why the closest incumbent meters at 15 documents for $19. At $15/mo with zero marginal cost, gross margin is ~100% minus Stripe fees and static hosting.
autonomy_case: A1 self-serve: card-swipe web app, no demo, no call, and no security questionnaire — there is no data-processing agreement to negotiate when no document bytes are transmitted. A2 fulfilment by code: the deliverable is a file the user's own browser produced. A3 no human escalation, and this is the design centre — every candidate span is shown with class and confidence before export; low-confidence spans are surfaced in a 'review these' queue rather than silently applied or silently dropped; the export step runs a round-trip verifier that re-extracts text from the produced PDF and re-runs detection, and if any identifier survives it refuses to deliver the vector file and forces the rasterize path; a signed redaction log listing every applied box, its class and its confidence ships alongside the file. The product never asserts 'this filing is compliant' — it asserts 'here is what I found, here is what I could not verify, and here is proof that what I applied actually removed the underlying text.' Compliance certification stays with the attorney, which is both legally correct and the reason no human of ours is ever in the loop. A4 reference data self-maintains: the CourtListener bulk corpus regenerates on a fixed quarterly calendar and the injection generator is code, so the training distribution refreshes on a cron with no human curation; the deterministic recognizers key off checksum algorithms (Luhn, ABA) that do not change. A5 unattended ops: static asset hosting plus Stripe plus a licence-check endpoint — no document pipeline, no queue, no GPU fleet to babysit. A6 zero human minutes per customer: nothing to onboard, and support questions are pre-answered by the in-product review UI showing exactly what was and was not found.
pricing_hypothesis: Free: unlimited local detection and on-screen preview, export capped at 3 documents/month — the free tier is generous precisely because inference costs nothing, and it converts at the export step, which is the moment of value. Solo: $15/month or $144/year, unlimited documents, unlimited pages, redaction log included. Firm: $39/month for 5 seats. The headline is 'unlimited', which Redactable structurally cannot match at $19-for-15-documents because their marginal cost is real and ours is zero — that asymmetry, not a feature list, is the pitch.
distribution: Zero-human channels. SEO against the exact anxiety, which is already a search phrase people type: 'redact PDF without uploading it', 'redact PDF offline', 'FRCP 5.2 redaction checklist', 'HIPAA de-identification 18 identifiers tool', plus head-to-head comparison pages (vs Redactable, vs Acrobat's manual redact, vs Presidio-for-non-developers) where the incumbents' own cloud-processing disclosure is the wedge copy. Free-tier wedge: unlimited detection and preview makes the tool worth linking to even unpaid, which is what earns forum links. Communities where this buyer already complains about the job: r/LawFirm, r/Lawyertalk, r/paralegal, r/therapists, state-bar practice-management listservs, legal-tech newsletters. Product Hunt launch on the privacy claim. A published, dated eval report (per-class recall, methodology, held-out sets) is itself a linkable SEO asset no incumbent publishes. AP1 ASSISTANT SHADOW — why ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini at $0-20/mo does not swallow this: the job is defined by the prohibition on uploading. A privileged exhibit or a therapy record cannot be pasted into a consumer assistant; that prohibition IS the purchase. Beyond admissibility, the assistant returns prose rather than character offsets and bounding boxes across 200 scanned pages, cannot rewrite a PDF content stream to delete glyphs, and cannot re-open its own output to prove the text is gone. Batch scale (thousands of spans per case file, not one paragraph), embedding at the exact point of work, structured span output flowing into a file rewrite, and a vertical eval a generalist cannot be certified on — all four acceptable answers apply. AP2 BROWSER SHADOW — Gemini in Chrome and agentic browsers read and act on pages; they do not rewrite a local PDF's content stream, cannot guarantee non-transmission (transmission is their value proposition), and produce no signed redaction log. This is not 'explain/summarize/act on this page' for a general user; it is file surgery for a user whose defining requirement is that no page ever leaves.
risks: AP6 platform risk is deliberately near-zero and that is a feature: no frontier model vendor to deprecate or reprice (weights are self-hosted ONNX we fine-tuned), no lab ToS, and no Chrome Web Store — shipping as a web app rather than an extension dodges store review, extension permission warnings and policy churn entirely. Residual platform exposure is browser capability: Firefox still has WebGPU disabled by default and Safari desktop 26.0+ is only partial (https://caniuse.com/webgpu, fetched 2026-08-20), so a WASM q8 fallback is mandatory and will be several times slower on long scanned files. NOT YET PROVEN, in order of danger: (1) the buyer population is unsourced — I could not fetch a count of US solo practitioners or small practices today because the session's search budget was exhausted; validation must establish it before build. (2) True glyph removal client-side is genuinely hard — deleting text runs from a PDF content stream without corrupting the file is fiddly, and the rasterize fallback costs searchability and file size; this is the single biggest engineering risk and should be spiked first, before any other work. (3) Recall on adversarial real-world scans (handwritten annotations, stamps, tables, faxed 200dpi) is currently asserted from a synthetic distribution and must be measured against a real held-out set before any recall number is published. (4) Willingness to pay: this buyer already owns Acrobat, and 'find it for me' may not be worth $15/mo to someone who redacts four documents a year — the free tier's export cap is the experiment that answers this. (5) Malpractice framing: the product must never be marketed as guaranteeing compliance; if positioning slips from assistive to certifying, the legal exposure is real, and the A3 design (review queue, signed log, refusal-to-export) is the mitigation that must not be softened to raise conversion.
